challenges.name: packages-go-test-quiz
challenges.title: Check it: exported names, internal packages and t.Fatalf
challenges.description: Decide which names another package can use, and predict how much of a failing table test go test reports.

questions.explanation: A name is exported, and so usable from other packages, exactly when it starts with an upper-case letter. phone.Normalize and phone.ErrInvalid are exported, and cmd/notifier is inside the same module root that contains internal/, so it may import the package. onlyDigits starts with a lower-case letter: from another package the compiler says "undefined: phone.onlyDigits". The same rule applies to struct fields: n.Country is visible, n.digits is not. And internal/ is enforced by the go command: only code inside the tree rooted at the parent of internal (here the trackd module) may import it, so a different module gets "use of internal package saigonparcel.vn/trackd/internal/phone not allowed".

options.text: In trackd/cmd/notifier, with n of type phone.Number: fmt.Println(n.digits)
In another module, saigonparcel.vn/billing, that requires trackd: import "saigonparcel.vn/trackd/internal/phone"

questions.explanation: t.Fatalf records the failure and stops the test function that is running - here TestNormalizeLoop itself, because there are no subtests. The loop never reaches cases 3 and 4, so go test prints one message, for case 2, and FAIL. Case 3 is just as broken but stays hidden until case 2 is fixed. t.Errorf would have recorded the failure and continued. Wrapping the body in t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) { ... }) gives every case its own subtest: t.Fatalf then stops only that subtest, and go test reports both failing cases (and, with -v, a PASS line for each passing one). That is why table-driven tests use t.Run.

options.text: Two failures, for case 2 and case 3, then FAIL
One failure, for case 2, then FAIL: the test stops at the first t.Fatalf
One failure, for case 3: t.Fatalf only reports the last failure
Nothing: t.Fatalf inside a loop is a compile error

challenges.name: fix-normalize-phone
challenges.title: Fix normalizePhone until every row of the table passes
challenges.description: After the weekend incident, normalizePhone accepts +84 numbers again. Customer support has since sent more rows for the test table, and several still fail: numbers written 84 90 123 4567 without the plus are rejected, numbers with letters typed into them are accepted, and a landline number gets an SMS that can never arrive. Fix normalizePhone so it follows the SMS gateway's rules written at the top of the file: only digits, spaces, dots, dashes and one leading plus are allowed; the number is 0, 84 or +84 followed by 9 digits; the 9 digits start with 3, 5, 7, 8 or 9; the result is +84 and the 9 digits. The test runner works like a table-driven test: it reads RAW|WANT rows and prints ok or FAIL for each.
